subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a persistent `tui.accessibility.plainText` mode with canonical ASCII semantics and a configurable pi-tui selector prefix?
rationale: The accessibility need and affected paths are established, but repository policy requires explicit approval for a new config surface and maintainers must choose whether selector ownership belongs upstream or locally.

options.title: Approve persistent TUI mode
options.body: Add `tui.accessibility.plainText`, scope it to all TUI presentation paths from startup, and add the selector-prefix seam upstream or through an intentionally maintained local abstraction.

options.title: Use a CLI-only launch flag
options.body: Add an ASCII launch flag without persistent config, reducing schema growth but requiring affected users to supply it on every launch.

options.title: Defer the presentation contract
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a broader terminal presentation-profile system is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve persistent TUI mode
recommendation.body: Add `tui.accessibility.plainText`, scope it to all TUI presentation paths from startup, and add the selector-prefix seam upstream or through an intentionally maintained local abstraction.

likelyOwner.reason: The original TUI and centralized tool-display behavior date to his commits, and he remains the strongest recent contributor spanning the affected owner boundary.
